title: Fix ISO week number calculation at year boundaries
prompt: The function iso_week(date_str) in starter/iso_week.py accepts an ISO date string (YYYY-MM-DD) and returns a tuple (iso_year, week_number) using the ISO 8601 definition. The starter uses the wrong strftime directives: it uses %Y (calendar year) instead of %G (ISO year) and %W (Monday-based week, 0-indexed) instead of %V (ISO week number). This causes wrong results at year boundaries. Fix it so that iso_week('2024-12-30') == (2025, 1), iso_week('2025-01-01') == (2025, 1), iso_week('2023-01-01') == (2022, 52). Do not edit the tests.

grader_files.test_iso_week.py:
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "starter"))

from iso_week import iso_week


def test_year_boundary_end():
    # 2024-12-30 is in ISO week 1 of 2025
    assert iso_week("2024-12-30") == (2025, 1)


def test_year_boundary_start():
    # 2025-01-01 is in ISO week 1 of 2025
    assert iso_week("2025-01-01") == (2025, 1)


def test_prior_year_week():
    # 2023-01-01 is in ISO week 52 of 2022
    assert iso_week("2023-01-01") == (2022, 52)


def test_midyear():
    # 2024-07-15 is in ISO week 29 of 2024
    assert iso_week("2024-07-15") == (2024, 29)


def test_normal_start():
    # 2024-01-08 is in ISO week 2 of 2024
    assert iso_week("2024-01-08") == (2024, 2)
